## Three capability states, and `missing` needs positive evidence

`available` when a model's profile says `supported`, its operation is `supported`+`enabled`, and at least one of the profile's own postable routes is `enabled` (a role-gated id additionally needs one postable route carrying its whole `REQUIRED_ROLES` set as `supported`); `missing` only when a profile or operation says no, or when at least one postable route is open, every open postable route refuses at least one required role (or carries it only past a zero count bound), and no postable declaration is itself undecided; and only when every model says so — one model refusing while another does not mention the operation (or lists no operation at all) is `unknown`, because that silent model may serve, the same way one model granting it is enough for `available`; `unknown` for everything else — failed request, absent field, `unknown` enum value, unconfirmed reachability, an untranslatable declaration, or a capability no profile can express. `resolve()` also returns `reasons`, which names the kind of refusal for every `missing` capability: `unsupported` (the model refused), `endpoint_disabled` (the deployment closed the operation's routes) or `route_disabled` (every postable route the profile declares is closed). Reasons for `unknown` live in `unresolved` (declaration level) or in `UNROUTED` (capability level).

## Status and reason mapping (the contract)

Every row below is read with the profile saying `supported` and its operation saying `supported` + `enabled`. A profile whose own `support` is `unknown` under an enabled operation is `unknown` with no note, and an operation whose `exposure` is `unknown` is `unknown` the same way; an operation that says `unsupported`, or is `disabled`, still decides the row on its own, because a refusal needs no profile evidence.

| Upstream declaration | status | where the reason lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| profile `support=unsupported` | `missing` | `reasons[cid] = "unsupported"` |
| operation `support=unsupported` | `missing` | `reasons[cid] = "unsupported"` |
| operation `supported` + `exposure=disabled` | `missing` | `reasons[cid] = "endpoint_disabled"` |
| every route the profile can post to is `exposure=disabled` | `missing` | `reasons[cid] = "route_disabled"` |
| every postable route the profile declares is `disabled`, beside a route this table cannot place (`/v1/videos/sync`, the socket, an unrecognised path) whatever its own `exposure` says | `missing` | `reasons[cid] = "route_disabled"`; the unplaceable route is `unresolved: route_mismatch` / `unknown_route`, a diagnostic only |
| every postable route the profile declares is `exposure=unknown` | `unknown` | `unresolved: exposure_unknown`, one per distinct `(profile, route)` — reachability unconfirmed, not a refusal |
| profile declares no postable route (`routes: []`, no usable `path`, or only routes this tool never posts to) | `unknown` | `unresolved: no_route_declared` |
| a route entry with no usable `transport`/`method`/`path`, or a `routes` value that is not a list, with no usable postable route beside it | `unknown` | `unresolved: malformed_route` — the path is named when it can be read; `no_route_declared` too when that leaves no postable route |
| an unrecognised path, and nothing else usable | `unknown` | `unresolved: unknown_route`, and `no_route_declared` because no postable route is declared |
| another operation's path, or a wrong method/transport, with no usable postable route beside it | `unknown` | `unresolved: route_mismatch`, and `no_route_declared` when that leaves no usable postable route |
| upstream profile, no id here, declared on an open postable route | `unknown` | `unresolved: no_local_capability` — a closed or undecided route on that profile says nothing about it |
| profile supported, at least one postable route is open, but none declares the id's whole `REQUIRED_ROLES` set as `supported` — a role is absent, split across routes, or refused on one route while another is silent | `unknown` | `unresolved: role_not_declared` |
| a postable route whose `exposure` is absent, unreadable or the literal `unknown`, when that doubt is why the id stays `unknown` | `unknown` | `unresolved: exposure_unknown`, one per distinct `(profile, route)` |
| a `profiles[]` element whose id cannot be read, or a `profiles` value that is not a list | no evidence from that profile | `unresolved: malformed_profile`, once per operation |
| an `operations[<op>]` value that is not an object | no evidence from that operation | `unresolved: malformed_operation`, once per operation |
| profile supported, at least one postable route is open and every open postable route refuses at least one required role — one role refused everywhere, or two routes each refusing a different one, whether or not they mention the other roles (`REQUIRED_ROLES`) — with no postable declaration left undecided | `missing` | `reasons[cid] = "unsupported"` |
| profile supported, a required role declared `support=supported` with `max_count: 0` on every open postable route that could carry it | `missing` | `reasons[cid] = "unsupported"` — the tool sends one item, a zero bound cannot take it |
| …the same, but a route this table cannot place names a required role as `supported` | `missing` | `reasons[cid] = "unsupported"` — an unplaceable route cannot rescue the refusal; it stays `unresolved: route_mismatch` / `unknown_route` |
| unknown operation / profile / misplaced profile | no evidence → `unknown` | `unresolved: unmapped_stage` / `unknown_profile` / `operation_mismatch` |
| `supported`, `enabled`, one `enabled` postable route (role-gated ids: one postable route carrying all `REQUIRED_ROLES` as `supported`) | `available` | none for the verdict — a diagnostic note may still sit in `unresolved` |
| a capability no upstream profile can express | `unknown` | `UNROUTED[cid]` (`no_upstream_profile` / `no_upstream_operation` / `parameter_only` / `no_local_adapter`) |
| no answer (`None`, no `models`, `models` not a list) | all `unknown` | `endpoint = "absent"` |
| answered, but no model declared an operation | all `unknown` | `endpoint = "empty"` |
| answered in another contract — `object` or `schema_version` is not `omni.capabilities` / `1` | all `unknown`, `models` never read | `endpoint = "unreadable"` + `unresolved: unsupported_format` |
| operation answered with `profiles: []` | `unknown` | `endpoint = "present"` |
| one model refuses, another does not mention that operation | `unknown` | none — the silent model may serve, so the refusal is not deployment-wide; a model that lists **no** operation at all is `unresolved: malformed_model` instead |
| a `models[]` element that is not a model — not an object, no `operations` object, or an empty one | no evidence from it; its silence keeps the affected ids `unknown` | `unresolved: malformed_model` (reported once, only when another model declared something) |

One boundary is left, and it now cuts the other way: a route this table cannot place is a diagnostic and never a channel — an unrecognised path, `/v1/videos/sync` or the socket cannot void a profile that answered, cannot keep a refusal undecided, and cannot turn "every postable route disabled" into anything but `missing` with `route_disabled`, whatever its own `exposure` says. What does keep a row undecided is a postable route whose `exposure` is absent, unreadable or the literal `unknown`: that route is one this tool can still post to, so the doubt is real, while the same doubt on an unplaceable route is nobody's channel. The three verdict notes — `exposure_unknown`, `no_route_declared`, `role_not_declared` — are attributed once the cross-model aggregate is known, and only to a `(operation, profile)` pair that still has an `unknown` capability id: a profile with no id here gets the shape reasons instead when it declares a route to report (`route_mismatch`, `malformed_route`, `unknown_route`, or `no_local_capability` while that route is open) and nothing at all when it declares none, because there is no id for a verdict note to explain. And `endpoint` distinguishes "did not answer" (`absent`) from "answered without declaring" (`empty`) from "declared" (`present`) from "answered in a contract this table does not read" (`unreadable`). Both keys are compared as published — `object` is the string `"omni.capabilities"`, `schema_version` the integer `1`, so `"1"` is a different shape and not the same version. A body that names neither key is read as v1 instead of being refused: upstream's response model always emits both, so a missing envelope cannot be told apart from a v1 body a proxy stripped. The gate runs before the `absent` / `empty` states, so a body with a foreign envelope is `unreadable` even when it carries no `models` at all, and `topology` comes back empty with it: `stages[]` of the refused body is the same unreviewed shape as its `models`. `declarations()` applies the same gate and returns `None`, so the two readers cannot disagree about one body.

So `video.first_frame` and `video.edit` carry `REQUIRED_ROLES`, and a `yes` verdict survives only when **one** of the profile's own open postable routes declares **every** one of those roles with `support=supported` in `request.inputs` (a closed route, or a path this operation does not own, counts for nothing). Otherwise the id is `unknown`, or `missing` once every open postable route refuses at least one of those roles. `support` alone is not the whole answer: the count window published beside it (`min_count` / `max_count`, both optional inclusive counts) is part of it. The tool sends one item, so `support=supported` with `max_count: 0` is a refusal in effect — a role capped at zero cannot carry it — and `min_count: 2` is one too, because that one item cannot satisfy the minimum. An absent bound is no bound on that side; a bound that is not a whole number leaves the entry undecided rather than guessed. One route, not the union of them: a request leaves on a single route, so `source_video` declared on `/v1/videos` beside the two noise masks on `/v1/videos/sync` is not an edit request either route would accept — that stays `unknown` with `role_not_declared`. Upstream publishes those four roles as of `b934b642` (head `12d834c2`): Wan I2V declares `first_frame` supported with `min_count: 0` / `max_count: 1` beside a required `image` — the same supplied image, so the two counts are not additive — and both VACE architectures declare `first_frame` `unsupported` with `max_count: 0` on every profile they publish; the editing roles (`source_video`, `video_noise_mask`, `audio_noise_mask`) are declared supported with `min_count: 0` / `max_count: 1` where the handler accepts latent-mask editing, and `unsupported` with `max_count: 0` where it does not. So `video.first_frame` reads `available` on Wan I2V and `missing` with `unsupported` on VACE, and `video.edit` reads `missing` with `unsupported` where those roles are refused — with no code change, because the gate reads the declaration rather than a written-in role list. A body that publishes modality roles only still leaves both ids `unknown`, and the report says why with `role_not_declared`. When at least one postable route is open and every open postable route refuses at least one required role, the document has said no — one role refused everywhere, or two routes each refusing a different one, even when neither route mentions the other roles — and the id is `missing` with `reasons[cid] = "unsupported"`, exactly like a refusing profile: "the deployment will not take that input" is a different fact from "the document does not say", and it needs a different fix. A declared route this table cannot place — `/v1/videos/sync`, the socket, an unrecognised path — is reported and nothing more: whatever its own `exposure` says, it cannot keep the answer open. Only one of the profile's own postable routes with an absent, unreadable or `unknown` exposure is a channel this tool can still use; unless another reference to that same path is declared `enabled`, it keeps the answer `unknown`.
